correctness.rationale: With H=L²(0,1)=U⊕V split by integer Fourier indices J, synthesis T_J(u+v)=u+M_θv has Gram [[I,C],[C*,I]] where C=P_U M_θ P_V. The multiplier circle arc admits the exact scalar center c=e^{iπθ}cos(πθ) at operator-norm distance sin(π|θ|); hence ‖C‖≤sin(π|θ|) and the squared Riesz bounds follow for all partitions. Output triangularity yields D=P_V M_θ|V with numerical range rotated into Re≥cos(πθ)>0; the same for D* proves D and T_J invertible, so both frame and Riesz interpretations hold. For J=nonnegative integers, the cross operator is sin(πθ)/π times shifted Hilbert H_{1−θ}; coefficient vectors (j+1)^−1/2 show its norm≥π via double-integral asymptotic π log N, matching ≤π, proving simultaneous sharpness. Supercritical |θ|>1/2 gives a Hardy-function annihilator; at equality regularized (1−rz)^−1/2 is an approximate annihilator with diverging L² norm and bounded defect. The local independently built Hilbert matrices of sizes 12,24,48,96,192 at θ=.3 have strictly increasing largest eigenvalues <π. These finite checks do not establish the Hilbert norm or critical singularity, which require the given analysis.

value.rationale: Worst-partition stability of two natural modulated Fourier bases is a central quantitative weaving problem. Explicit optimal uniform constants, saturation by a canonical one-sided partition and a sharp singularity at half-phase provide a reusable spectral condition model. The exact envelope is not just Kadets existence or a rephrased perturbation bound; the cross-Hilbert norm sharpness and frame invertibility matter.

limitations: All integer Fourier modes split in two arbitrary parts and real phase |θ|<1/2, with explicit obstruction for 1/2≤|θ|<1; no general weights or multidimensional universality.
One-sided saturation is an infinite coefficient-sequence limit; no finite-vector attainment is claimed.
